Prevention: This disease is spread by infected stem cuttings, so use healthy planting materials obtained from plants without symptoms of the disease (cankers, stems with insect holes and stem dieback).
Stem cuttings can be treated with a fungicide before planting to protect against the disease (see yellow direct control)
Directorates or approved multiplications sites across the country
Avoid planting on the same piece of land for more than 3 seasons, rotate with grains
Remove old cassava plant debris after harvest and burn
The pathogen infects through wounds and insect damage - so avoid wounding plants.
Late planting (second half of rainy season) can restrict disease associated with insect damage.
Monitoring: Monitor cassava fields at weekly interval after sprouting through to plant maturity.
Look for symptoms such as wilting, dieback and cankers especially in the wet season.
When symptoms are observed take action
Direct Control: Rogue out any infected plants as soon as symptoms can be seen to prevent the spread of the disease.
Restrictions: When using a pesticide or botanical, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
